An unknown ID, or an ID or flag for a suite the run leaves out, is a usage error (exit cod
e `2`) before anything runs.\n\nThe OAuth suite signs in on its own. When the server needs a sign-in for the other suites too, giv

e them a token, for example from `oauth login --credentials-out`:

--
| `--case <id>` | every enabled case | Run only this exac
t case id. Repeatable. |\n| `--server <name=url>` | | Bind a target server to an HTTP(S) URL. Repeatable. Split on the first `=`;
duplicate or unknown names are usage errors. |\n| `--mcp-config <path>` | | Explicit MCP JSON config, consulted before `./.mcp.jso
n` and `./.mcpjam/mcp.json`. A missing or invalid file fails setup. |\n| `--host <template>` | none | Emulate one host template's

handshake and settings. Never launches the real client. |
| `--inference <mode>` | `auto` | `auto`, `byok` or `mcpjam`. |
--
Global `--timeout` bounds each setup operation and MCP request, not the whole run. Exit codes: `0` passed, `1` failed, `2` usage/u
nsupported/import/policy, `3` credentials, `4` setup/billing/artifact, `5` inconclusive or interrupted; see [Exit codes](https://d

ocs.mcpjam.com/cli/local-evals.md#exit-codes).

***

--
`--host` as a deprecated spelling of `--client`. Passing both `--clie

nt` and
`--host` is a usage error rather than a silent precedence rule.

### Editing safely: `configId` and `expectedConfigId`\

n
--

Launch a goal run. **Spends model credits**: fans out into `targets × iterations` chat sessions.

| Flag | Required | D

escription |
| - | - | - |
--
| `--idempotency-key <key>` | No | Replay guard: a retry with the same key returns the run alread
y started and starts no second runner |\n| `--expected-sponsored <n>` | No | How many of this launch's conversations you expect to
be sponsored (paid from MCPJam's per-user allowance instead of your organization's credits). If the actual split differs, the lau

nch is refused with a `409` and nothing is created. Omit to accept whatever split applies. |

***

--

Each pending request
holds one of the account's five concurrent-connection slots for up to an hour. If `connect` reports `ACTIVE_REQUEST_LIMIT`, the er
ror details include the ids of the open requests; cancel the abandoned ones with `connect-cancel` to free slots.\n\n### `cloud pro

jects servers connect-status`

--
| `--project <id-or-name>` | No | Project name or ID |
| `--limit <n>` | No | Revisions per

page, 1 to 200 (default 50) |
| `--cursor <cursor>` | No | `nextCursor` from the previous page |

### `cloud projects servers r

evision`
--

Grade a saved server against a publisher's directory as the platform reaches it, through the saved server row and
the authorize exchange. This is the hosted half of `readiness check`: it answers a different question (what the platform sees, not
what your machine sees), can optionally run a model for experience observations (included with MCPJam; no credits are consumed),
and leaves a persistent record.\n\nAll `readiness` hosted commands require an `sk_` API key (via `--api-key` or the `MCPJAM_API_KE

Y` environment variable) or a prior `mcpjam cloud login`.

--
The `mcpjam` CLI is two invocations. Local MCP testing stays at t
he top level: inspect, debug, and test MCP servers from the command line or CI (connectivity, OAuth, MCP Apps, tools/resources/pro
mpts, protocol conformance). Most local commands are one-shot; `mcpjam mcp` and `subscriptions listen` keep a process open. Accoun
t-bound commands live under `mcpjam cloud` and talk to your MCPJam account. There are no compatibility aliases for the old Cloud p
aths; see [Migrating to CLI 4.0](https://docs.mcpjam.com/cli/migration.md).\nThese stay at the program root. They reject `--api-ke
y` / `--api-url` / `--project`, except `test`, which accepts them only to reach MCPJam-hosted inference.\n| [`readiness`](https://
docs.mcpjam.com/cli/reference#readiness-hosted-commands) | Grade a server against a publisher's directory. Hosted `start` / `statu
s` / `list` / `cancel` / `report` stay here (leaf `--api-key`; no Cloud project link) | `check`, `start claude`, `start openai`, `
start muse`, `status`, `list`, `cancel`, `report` |\nAccount-bound commands. Declare `--api-key` / `--api-url` on `mcpjam cloud` (
before or after descendants). `mcpjam oauth login` is MCP-server OAuth; `mcpjam cloud login` is your MCPJam account.\n| [`cloud ev
al`](https://docs.mcpjam.com/cli/reference#cloud-eval-commands) | Author and run eval suites in your hosted MCPJam projects | `cre
ate`, `list`, `run`, `status` |\n| [`cloud tunnel`](https://docs.mcpjam.com/cli/reference#cloud-tunnel) | Expose a local MCP serve
r through a public MCPJam tunnel URL, registered as a server in your project | `tunnel --server <name> <url>`, `tunnel --server <n
ame> -- <command>` |\n| [`cloud clients`](https://docs.mcpjam.com/cli/reference#cloud-clients-commands) | Manage clients in your h
osted MCPJam projects (`cloud hosts` is a deprecated alias) | `list`, `get`, `create`, `update`, `servers`, `duplicate`, `delete`,
`templates` |\n| [`cloud environments`](https://docs.mcpjam.com/cli/reference#cloud-environments-commands) | Manage project envir
onments, the host and server bundles eval suites and goals run against | `list`, `get`, `resolve`, `archive`, `ensure-adhoc` |\n|
[`cloud projects servers`](https://docs.mcpjam.com/cli/reference#cloud-projects-servers-commands) | Connect MCP servers to a proje
ct and manage pending connection requests | `connect`, `connect-status`, `connect-cancel` |\n## Cloud credentials and API URL", "s
